'''Tomás Cano''' (born 4 January 1961) is a Spanish and Andorran ski jumper who competed primarily for Spain. He holds the Andorran national record and is a former Spanish [[List of national ski-jumping records|national record holder]] in ski jumping.<ref name="janiket">{{cite web |last= |first= |date=24 January 1979 |title=Edición del miércoles, 24 enero 1979 |trans-title=Edition of Wednesday, 24 January 1979 |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1979/01/24/pagina-35/1035291/pdf.html?search=Tom%C3%A1s%20Cano |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326002808/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1979/01/24/pagina-35/1035291/pdf.html?search=Tom%C3%A1s%20Cano |archive-date=26 March 2014 |access-date= |website=El Mundo Deportivo |page=35 |language=es}}</ref> Cano achieved 2nd place in the King's Cup in 1981 and was a Spanish national champion.

From 1979 to 1983, he competed in the [[FIS Ski Jumping World Cup|World Cup]] but never earned points in the overall standings, with his best result being 48th place. He participated in the [[Four Hills Tournament]] three times, with his highest finish being 72nd in the [[1978–79 Four Hills Tournament|27th edition]], which was not yet part of the World Cup.<ref name="profil">{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=FIS-Ski – Biography – CANO Thomas |url=https://www.fis-ski.com/DB/general/athlete-biography.html?sector=JP&competitorid=8651&type=result |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=fis-ski.com |language=de}}</ref> He also competed in the 1982 World Championships, finishing 56th on the normal hill and 48th on the large hill. Cano participated in the [[FIS Nordic Junior World Ski Championships|Junior World Championships]] and the [[FISU World University Games]] without notable success. He earned points in several [[FIS Ski Jumping Europa Cup|Europa Cup]] events.

Cano was the only Andorran representative in official international competitions, earning one point for Andorra in the European Cup in 1992 at [[La Molina (ski resort)|La Molina]].

He used skis manufactured by [[Elan (company)|Elan]].<ref name="mihi">{{cite web |last= |first= |date=26 March 1979 |title=Edición del lunes, 26 marzo 1979 |trans-title=Edition of Monday, 26 March 1979 |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1979/03/26/pagina-29/1038129/pdf.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326002706/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1979/03/26/pagina-29/1038129/pdf.html |archive-date=26 March 2014 |access-date= |website=El Mundo Deportivo |pages=28–29 |language=es}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Spain ===

==== Early career and first competitions ====
Originally from [[Elche]], Cano later moved to [[Catalonia]].<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date=1 September 2011 |title=Saltos de esquí en España – El Equipo Español de saltos |trans-title=Ski Jumping in Spain – The Spanish Ski Jumping Team |url=http://www.nevasport.com/retro-ski/art/33180/Saltos-de-esqui-en-Espana-El-Equipo-Espanol-de-saltos/ |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=nevasport.com |language=es}}</ref> As a student, he trained primarily on Swiss and Spanish ski jumps.<ref name="janiket"/> One of his earliest international competitions was the Grand Prix in [[Frenštát pod Radhoštěm]], Czechoslovakia, on 11 September 1977, where he finished last in 93rd place with two 50-meter jumps, earning the lowest score of the event. The winner was {{Interlanguage link|František Novák|pl|František Novák}}.<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Frenstat CZE 1977.09.11 GP Fr |url=http://www.wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl/Konkurs.aspx?season=1978&id=1931 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl |language=pl}}</ref><ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA">{{cite web |last=Kwieciński |first=Adam |date= |title=CANO Thomas 1961.01.04 SPA |url=http://www.wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl/Zawodnik.aspx?name=CANO%20Thomas |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl |language=pl}}</ref>

In 1978, Cano competed in the Junior World Championships in [[Murau]], finishing 46th out of 52 competitors with jumps of 49 and 57 meters on the normal hill.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kwieciński |first=Adam |title=Murau AUT 1978.03.12 MSJun |trans-title=Murau AUT 1978.03.12 Junior World Championships |website=wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl |language=pl |date= |url=http://www.wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl/Konkurs.aspx?season=1978&id=19 |access-date=19 September 2025}}</ref> He also competed in the 1979 Junior World Championships in Canada, placing 44th on the normal hill, ahead of only three classified competitors.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kwieciński |first=Adam |title=Quebec CAN 1979.02.18 MSJun |trans-title=Quebec CAN 1979.02.18 Junior World Championships |website=wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl |language=pl |date= |url=http://www.wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl/Konkurs.aspx?season=1979&id=19 |access-date=19 September 2025}}</ref> A week earlier, in [[Lake Placid, New York|Lake Placid]], he finished last in 48th place with jumps of 70 and 69 meters, where [[Pentti Kokkonen]] won.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kwieciński |first=Adam |date= |title=Lake Placid USA 1979.02.10 |url=http://www.wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl/Konkurs.aspx?season=1979&id=1507 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl |language=pl}}</ref>

Cano was the first Spaniard to compete in the [[Four Hills Tournament]], participating in the 1978–79 season. He placed in the bottom eight in all events: 77th in [[Oberstdorf]],<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=30.12.1978 – Oberstdorf (RFN) K-90 |url=http://www.skokinarciarskie.pl/index.php?a=wyniki&b=wyniki&cykl=tcs&sezon=1978/1979&konkurs_id=2015&seria=2 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=skokinarciarskie.pl |language=pl}}</ref> 77th in [[Garmisch-Partenkirchen]] (the lowest score),<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=01.01.1979 – Garmisch-Partenkirchen (RFN) K-90 |url=http://www.skokinarciarskie.pl/index.php?a=wyniki&b=wyniki&cykl=tcs&sezon=1978/1979&konkurs_id=2016&seria=1 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=skokinarciarskie.pl |language=pl}}</ref> 74th in [[Innsbruck]],<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=04.01.1979 – Innsbruck (Austria) K-90 |url=http://www.skokinarciarskie.pl/index.php?a=wyniki&b=wyniki&cykl=tcs&sezon=1978/1979&konkurs_id=2017&seria=2 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=skokinarciarskie.pl |language=pl}}</ref> and 72nd in [[Bischofshofen]], the second-to-last position.<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=06.01.1979 – Bischofshofen (Austria) K-90 |url=http://www.skokinarciarskie.pl/index.php?a=wyniki&b=wyniki&cykl=tcs&sezon=1978/1979&konkurs_id=2018&seria=2 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=skokinarciarskie.pl |language=pl}}</ref> He scored 359.8 points, finishing 72nd out of 84 competitors in the overall standings.<ref name="Skoki narciarskie Turniej">{{cite web |last= |first= |title=Skoki narciarskie – Turniej Czterech Skoczni 1978/1979 |trans-title=Ski Jumping – Four Hills Tournament 1978/1979 |website=skokinarciarskie.pl |language=pl |date= |url=http://www.skokinarciarskie.pl/index.php?a=cykle&b=sezon&cykl=tcs&sezon=1978/1979 |access-date=19 September 2025}}</ref>

On 25 March 1979, during a canceled round of the King's Cup in [[La Molina (ski resort)|La Molina]], Cano set a La Molina ski jump record of 70 meters. In the restarted round, he jumped 55 meters, finishing 19th, while Norwegian [[Johan Sætre]] broke his record and won the event.<ref name="mihi" /><ref name="La Molina">{{cite web |last= |first= |title=La Molina |website=skisprungschanzen.com |language=en |date= |url=http://www.skisprungschanzen.com/EN/Ski+Jumps/SPA-Spain/La+Molina/0096/ |access-date=19 September 2025}}</ref>

Cano debuted in the World Cup on 30 December 1979 in [[Oberstdorf]] during the Four Hills Tournament, jumping 85 meters and finishing 94th. This jump set a Spanish national record, likely surpassed in 1982 by [[José Rivera (ski jumper)|José Rivera]], who jumped 94.5 meters in Oberstdorf.<ref name="janiket"/> In 1978 or 1979, Cano won the Spanish national championship.<ref name="mihi"/>

==== 1980s ====
In 1980, Cano began the year with a Four Hills Tournament event in [[Garmisch-Partenkirchen]], jumping 72 meters and finishing 98th. In the subsequent events, he placed 105th and 104th, finishing 101st overall with 235.3 points, ahead of 14 competitors.<ref name="Skoki narciarskie Turniej2">{{cite web |last= |first= |title=Skoki narciarskie – Turniej Czterech Skoczni 1979/1980 |trans-title=Ski Jumping – Four Hills Tournament 1979/1980 |website=skokinarciarskie.pl |language=pl |date= |url=http://www.skokinarciarskie.pl/index.php?a=cykle&b=sezon&cykl=tcs&sezon=1979/1980 |access-date=19 September 2025}}</ref>

On 27 February 1980, he competed in the World Cup in [[St. Moritz]], placing 53rd with jumps of 65 and 75.5 meters. Two days later, in [[Gstaad]], he finished 57th (66.5 and 71 meters), and on 2 March in [[Engelberg]], he placed 61st (80 and 74 meters).<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/> That winter, he finished 6th in the King's Cup with 192.4 points.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=31 March 1980 |title=El noruego Saetre repitió triunfo |trans-title=Norwegian Saetre Repeated Victory |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1980/03/31/pagina-51/1056757/pdf.html# |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=51 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326001016/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1980/03/31/pagina-51/1056757/pdf.html |archive-date=26 March 2014}}</ref> In September, he competed again in [[Frenštát pod Radhoštěm]], finishing 54th.<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/>

The 1980–81 season began with World Cup events in Switzerland, where Cano placed 69th, 77th, and 67th, jumping 66, 61, and 72 meters, respectively.<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/> In early February 1981, he achieved a career highlight by finishing 2nd in the King's Cup with jumps of 69.5 and 67 meters,<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |date=2 February 1981 |title=Europeo de saltos en La Molina |trans-title=European Ski Jumping in La Molina |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1981/02/02/pagina-40/1068723/pdf.html# |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=40 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326000607/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1981/02/02/pagina-40/1068723/pdf.html |archive-date=26 March 2014}}</ref> earning 20 points in the [[FIS Ski Jumping Europa Cup|Europa Cup]] (predecessor to the [[FIS Ski Jumping Continental Cup|Continental Cup]]), his only podium in this series.<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |date=31 January 1983 |title=SUPERIORIDAD NORUEGA |trans-title=Norwegian Superiority |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1983/01/31/pagina-38/1101352/pdf.html# |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=38 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140325234025/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1983/01/31/pagina-38/1101352/pdf.html |archive-date=25 March 2014}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |date=7 February 1982 |title=VICTORIA DEL ITALIANO WEGHER |trans-title=Victory of the Italian Wegher |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1982/02/07/pagina-31/1079096/pdf.html# |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326002240/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1982/02/07/pagina-31/1079096/pdf.html |archive-date=26 March 2014}}</ref>

In late February 1981, Cano competed in the [[1981 Winter Universiade]], finishing 13th in the ski jumping event at Valle de Astún Ski Jump with jumps of 71 and 69 meters among 16 competitors.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=26 February 1981 |title=CLASIFICACIONES |trans-title=Classifications |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1981/02/26/pagina-35/1065546/pdf.html |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=35 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326003245/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1981/02/26/pagina-35/1065546/pdf.html |archive-date=26 March 2014}}</ref> That winter, he also won the Catalonia ski jumping championship with jumps of 51.9 and 62.7 meters.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=12 March 1981 |title=CANO, VENCEDOR ABSOLUTO |trans-title=Cano, Absolute Winner |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1981/03/12/pagina-31/1066182/pdf.html |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326002739/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1981/03/12/pagina-31/1066182/pdf.html |archive-date=26 March 2014}}</ref>

[[File:Oslo Holenkollen 1975.jpg|thumb|[[Holmenkollbakken]] in the summer of 1975. Cano achieved his best World Cup result (48th place) on this hill in 1982]]
In the 1981–82 season, Cano competed sparingly. In the European Cup, he placed 53rd in [[Seefeld in Tirol|Seefeld]] and 11th in [[La Molina (ski resort)|La Molina]]. At the 1982 World Championships, he finished 56th on the normal hill (63.5 and 67 meters, 165.5 points) and 48th on the large hill (82.5 and 84.5 meters, 168.8 points), events that were also part of the World Cup.<ref name="profil"/>

In the 1982–83 season, Cano had his most active international season. On 18 December 1982, he placed 50th in the World Cup in [[Cortina d'Ampezzo]] with a 66-meter jump. On 26 December, he finished 57th in the European Cup in [[St. Moritz]].<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/> He competed in the Four Hills Tournament for the third and final time, placing 77th in Oberstdorf (90.5 meters), 78th in Garmisch-Partenkirchen (80 meters), 88th in Innsbruck (72 meters), and 82nd in Bischofshofen (72 meters),<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA" /> finishing 78th overall with 291.8 points among 95 competitors.<ref name="Skoki narciarskie Turniej3">{{cite web |last= |first= |title=Skoki narciarskie – Turniej Czterech Skoczni 1982/1983 |trans-title=Ski Jumping – Four Hills Tournament 1982/1983 |website=skokinarciarskie.pl |language=pl |date= |url=http://www.skokinarciarskie.pl/index.php?a=cykle&b=sezon&cykl=tcs&sezon=1982/1983 |access-date=19 September 2025}}</ref> In four additional World Cup events in North America, his best result was 55th in Lake Placid on 15 January 1983.<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/>

In the European Cup, he competed in over 10 events, earning points twice: 9th in [[Saint-Nizier-du-Moucherotte|Saint-Nizier]] and 11th in La Molina. He was close to scoring in [[Chamonix]], finishing 16th. His final event of the season was on 3 April in [[Feldberg, Baden-Württemberg|Feldberg]], where he placed 36th with jumps of 77 and 75.5 meters.<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/>

In 1987, he finished 18th in the King's Cup in La Molina.<ref name="CANO Thomas 1961 01 04 SPA"/>

=== Andorra ===
Representing Andorra, Cano competed in the King's Cup on 3 February 1991, finishing 33rd out of 41 competitors with jumps of 58.5 and 60 meters.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=5 February 1991 |title=COPA DEL REY DE SALTOS |trans-title=King's Cup of Ski Jumping |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/02/05/pagina-47/1222683/pdf.html |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=47 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140325235244/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/02/05/pagina-47/1222683/pdf.html |archive-date=25 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Kwieciński |first=Adam |date= |title=La Molina SPA 1991.02.03 EC |url=http://www.wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl/Konkurs.aspx?season=1991&id=350 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl |language=pl}}</ref> In 1992, he placed 15th in the same event with jumps of 60.5 and 60 meters, earning 145.9 points and one point for Andorra in the European Cup standings.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kwieciński |first=Adam |date= |title=La Molina SPA 1992.01.26 EC |url=http://www.wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl/Konkurs.aspx?season=1992&id=352 |access-date=19 September 2025 |website=wyniki-skoki.hostingasp.pl |language=pl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cabanillas |first=Manuel |date=27 January 1992 |title=La Copa del Rey de saltos, para el galo Frenot |trans-title=The King's Cup of Ski Jumping, for the Frenchman Frenot |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1992/01/27/pagina-66/1251557/pdf.html |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=66 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326003053/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1992/01/27/pagina-66/1251557/pdf.html |archive-date=26 March 2014}}</ref> In the 1992 Spanish Championships, competing as an Andorran, he finished 4th with jumps of 64.5 and 62.5 meters, trailing medalists [[Bernat Sola]], {{Interlanguage link|Francisco Alegre|pl|Francisco Alegre}}, and Jesús Lobo by over 20 points.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=22 January 1992 |title=Bernat Solá, campió naciónal |trans-title=Bernat Solà, National Champion |url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1992/01/22/pagina-46/1243946/pdf.html |journal=El Mundo Deportivo |language=es |page=46 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140305095224/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1992/01/22/pagina-46/1243946/pdf.html |archive-date=5 March 2014}}</ref>
